rows.title: Refactor Owner Directory Structure for Component Separation
rows.excerpt:
### Current Implementation
The project structure places all classes related to pets, owners, and visits in a single directory. This organization can make the codebase harder to navigate and maintain as the project grows. To improve clarity and scalability, I propose refactoring the directory structure by segregating these classes into separate directories based on their functionality.

### Proposed Solution:
Create distinct directories for each component:

pets: For all pet-related classes and functionality.
owners: For all owner-related classes and functionality.
visits: For all visit-related classes and functionality.
Move the relevant classes and files into their respective directories.
Example:

Move Pet.java, PetController.java, etc., to the pets directory.
Move Owner.java, OwnerController.java, etc., to the owners directory.
Move Visit.java, VisitController.java, etc., to the visits directory.
Update imports throughout the project to reflect the new structure.

### Benefits:
Improved Readability: Each directory will contain only the files relevant to its component, making it easier for developers to find and understand code.
Better Scalability: As new features or functionality are added, the modular structure will help maintain organization.
Easier Maintenance: Fixes or updates related to a specific component can be implemented and tested more efficiently.

I recommend performing this refactoring as a separate commit to make the changes easier to track.
Let me know if there's any feedback or additional considerations before I start working on this!

rows.title: [Feature] Add search pets by name screen
rows.excerpt:
## Summary

Add a new screen that allows users to search for pets by name, similar to the existing "Find Owners" functionality.

## Motivation

- Currently there is no way to search for a pet directly by name; users must first find the owner and then browse their pets.
- A dedicated pet search screen would improve usability when the pet name is known but the owner is not.
- Aligns the pet entity with the same search UX pattern already established for owners.

## Proposed Solution

1. **New Thymeleaf template** (`templates/pets/findPets.html`) with a search form and results list/table.
2. **New controller** endpoint(s) in a `PetController` (or extend existing controller) to handle `GET /pets/find` and `GET /pets` with a `name` query parameter.
3. **New repository method** `findByNameContainingIgnoreCase(String name)` (or equivalent Spring Data query) in `PetRepository`.
4. **Navigation link** added to the main layout so users can access the pet search screen.
5. **Accessibility**: the new page must meet WCAG 2.2 Level AA (keyboard navigation, visible focus, proper labels, contrast, landmarks, etc.).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A "Find Pets" link is available in the main navigation menu
- [ ] Users can search for pets by entering a full or partial pet name (case-insensitive)
- [ ] An empty search returns all pets
- [ ] Search results display pet name, birth date, type, and owner name
- [ ] Clicking a result navigates to the pet's or owner's detail page
- [ ] The page is accessible (landmarks, labels, keyboard support, contrast)
- [ ] Unit and integration tests cover the new controller and repository methods
- [ ] Works with H2 (default), MySQL, and PostgreSQL profiles

## Alternatives Considered

- Extending the existing owner search to also filter by pet name — rejected because it conflates two different search intents.

## Additional Context

The implementation should follow the same patterns used by the existing "Find Owners" feature (`OwnerController`, `findOwners.html`, `ownersList.html`).

rows.title: Fix/add service documentation
rows.excerpt:
## Summary
Adds comprehensive Javadoc to `OwnerController`, `PetController`, and `VetController` — covering class descriptions, constructors, and all methods. No behavioural changes.

## The code issues
- **`OwnerController.java`** — Class description absent; 9 of 10 methods had no Javadoc. Only `showOwner` carried a minimal comment.
- **`PetController.java`** — Class description absent; 8 of 9 methods had no Javadoc. Only `updatePetDetails` was documented.
- **`VetController.java`** — Class description absent; all 4 methods and the constructor had no Javadoc.

## Why these matter
- **Maintainability**: undocumented method contracts force developers to read the full implementation to understand expected inputs, outputs, and error conditions, increasing the cost of every future change.
- **Onboarding**: controllers are the primary entry points into the application. New contributors encounter them first, yet had no inline guidance on routing behaviour, pagination conventions, or redirect semantics.
- **Tooling**: IDEs surface Javadoc as hover tooltips and in auto-generated API docs. Without it, developers lose the fastest path to understanding method contracts.

## What this PR does
- Adds a class-level description to each controller explaining its responsibility and base URL scope.
- Documents each constructor with `@param` tags describing injected dependencies and their roles.
- Documents each method with a description of its behaviour, `@param` tags for all parameters, `@return` for all non-void methods, and `@throws` where applicable.

## SonarQube findings addressed
| Rule  | File                   | Change                                              |
|-------|------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| S1176 | `OwnerController.java` | Javadoc added to class, constructor, and 9 methods  |
| S1176 | `PetController.java`   | Javadoc added to class, constructor, and 8 methods  |
| S1176 | `VetController.java`   | Javadoc added to class, constructor, and 4 methods  |

## Verification
- No logic was changed; all existing tests pass unchanged.
- Each Javadoc addition was committed individually to allow per-method review.

rows.title: Refactor: remove unnecessary imports and redundant intermediate variables
rows.excerpt:
## Summary
This PR removes unnecessary imports and eliminates redundant intermediate variables across three controllers and two test files, as part of the sustainable coding practices evaluation for SE754 Assignment 5.

## Problem
Manual inspection and SonarQube analysis identified two categories of redundant code across the `owner` package.

**Unnecessary imports** - `OwnerControllerTests.java` and `VetControllerTests.java` both had a class-level import for `MockMvcRequestBuilders` despite already having static imports for the individual methods (`get`, `post`) from the same class. This made the class-level import redundant and unused. Similarly, `OwnerController.java`, `PetController.java`, and `VisitController.java` each imported `java.util.Optional` which was only needed to hold an intermediate variable that was immediately unwrapped on the next line.

**Redundant intermediate variables** - In `OwnerController.java`, `PetController.java`, and `VisitController.java`, the pattern of assigning `owners.findById(...)` to an `optionalOwner` variable and then calling `.orElseThrow(...)` on the very next line served no purpose. SonarQube flags this under `java:S1488` - local variables should not be declared and then immediately returned or used.

## Changes
- Replaced `MockMvcRequestBuilders.post(...)` and `MockMvcRequestBuilders.get(...)` with the already-imported static equivalents in `OwnerControllerTests.java` and `VetControllerTests.java`, and removed the now-unused class-level imports
- Collapsed all `optionalOwner` intermediate variable declarations into single chained expressions using `.orElseThrow(...)` directly on the repository call in `OwnerController.java`, `PetController.java`, and `VisitController.java`
- Removed the `java.util.Optional` import from each controller where it was no longer referenced

## Sustainability Impact
Redundant code and unnecessary imports increase the noise developers must read through when understanding or modifying a file. Unused imports can mislead future contributors into thinking a type is meaningfully used, and they accumulate silently over time if not caught early.

- `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/OwnerController.java`
- `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/PetController.java`
